title: Throwing my hat into the ring: Here's Penpals, an experiment using AR face tracking to map webcam feeds onto player characters in VR chat-like environments.
author: sachasayan
selftext:
**Play it here:** [https://penpals.sachasayan.com](https://penpals.sachasayan.com). 

**Laptop (or webcam-enabled desktop) only.** 

Penpals is an experimental multiplayer game where your actual face, tracked live from your webcam, becomes your avatar’s face. Walk around the worlds with your friends, hear them through proximity voice, and take in their reactions when you pelt them with snowballs. 

**Some tech details for those interested:** 

* MediaPipe FaceMesh is used to track you locally in the browser, and an aligned photo crop with the eyes levelled, corrected exposure, and edges faded into a skin tone sampled from the player's cheeks is then mapped to their avatar. 
* Each client decides how much video it wants from each player. Nearby players get up to 350 kbps at 24 fps, distant ones 60 kbps at 6 fps at half resolution, and players you can’t see don’t send you video at all. 
* Yaw, pitch, roll and mouth openness also drive the avatar’s head, so nods and turns come through.
* Voice is spatial voice with HRTF panning, so people sound like they are where their avatar is!

**Toys:**

As a secondary experiment, there's also a lot of world-interactivity for a game of this size. Each world has a default toy (paintball guns, grappling hooks, snowballs), but there are dozens of other secondary toys and activities scattered around the game world too. You can roast marshmallows at a campfire in first person, ride cows, play capture the flag, fire cannons off the top of a castle, draw with chalk on sidewalks, ride ziplines... see if you can find them all! 

My favourite (and in-line with the theme of the game) is the face-swap ray: Hit a friend and you trade faces for a while — their live video ends up on your avatar and yours on theirs. Opus came up with this one. 

**Try it now:** [https://penpals.sachasayan.com](https://penpals.sachasayan.com)  


Happy to answer any questions in the comments!
